title: Factor-Graph SASCA and the Circuit-Size Prediction
summary: Current evaluations cover only divide-and-conquer leakage; formalizing analytical SASCA and testing the circuit-size prediction with a full-implementation factor graph remain open.

formal_statement.body: Existing investigations are limited to leakage samples exploitable by divide-and-conquer attacks that target independent key parts. Better formalize analytical SASCA attacks, and then analyze a SASCA that exploits a factor graph for a full masked implementation to determine to what extent it confirms the masking-security-proof prediction that an adversary's success rate is proportional to the target circuit size---the total amount of leakage samples---regardless of whether those samples correspond to enumerable intermediate computations.

scope.domain: Side-channel cryptanalysis of masked implementations using factor-graph SASCA.
parameters: Target circuit size (the total amount of leakage samples): the predicted scaling parameter for the adversary's success rate
scope.unresolved_remainder: Better formalize analytical SASCA attacks and determine whether a factor-graph SASCA on a full masked implementation confirms the predicted circuit-size proportionality regardless of whether leakage samples correspond to enumerable intermediate computations.

citations.label: Masking Proofs Are Tight and How to Exploit it in Security Evaluations

progress.summary: The source contrasts its divide-and-conquer-only evaluations with masking proofs predicting success proportional to total leakage. It explicitly presents full-implementation factor-graph SASCA analysis, preceded by better formalization, as an important open problem.
citation_labels: Vincent Grosso et al., Masking Proofs Are Tight and How to Exploit it in Security Evaluations
